content.jointProblem: Which combination of indexing-time and query-time Serbian script normalization can improve cross-script contract retrieval without unacceptable false matches or latency overhead? The first experiment would compare the existing PostgreSQL search with indexing-only, query-only, and combined normalization on an annotated sample of Latin, Cyrillic, mixed-script, and ambiguous contract queries, testing retrieval quality and response-time changes.

rationale.text: Rajić has evaluated rule-based normalization for Serbian orthographic variation, providing a relevant methodological starting point rather than a validated contract-search solution.

sources.quote: The paper describes a post-processing layer that applies rule-based normalization to the most frequent respelling patterns before tagging.

rationale.text: His work on regional lexical variants is relevant to investigating the company's dialect-related mapping ambiguities.

sources.quote: Rajić leads the work package on informal variant coverage, contributing the informal morphological variant lexicon developed in earlier work and coordinating its extension with Ijekavian and Bosnian lexical variants.

rationale.text: His corpus annotation and normalization project experience supports building a representative evaluation set and documenting difficult cases.

sources.quote: development of normalisation rules for 12 recurring orthographic variability patterns
The project also produced annotation guidelines revised through four internal calibration rounds

rationale.text: He has prior exposure to Serbian preprocessing for search relevance and to company text-data governance.

sources.quote: He has also provided informal consulting to one IT company in Novi Sad on preprocessing Serbian user-generated content for a search relevance task.
Rajić coordinated data-sharing agreements with four domestic companies to obtain pseudonymised customer communication text

constraints.text: Evaluation must cover both script directions, mixed-script documents, and ambiguous mappings; handling only uniformly scripted documents would not meet the task.

sources.quote: We want a solution that is robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones
there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.
users type a term in Latin script but the stored document uses Cyrillic, or vice versa

constraints.text: The prototype must be evaluated within the PostgreSQL full-text search workflow, with an agreed latency limit rather than an assumed performance improvement.

sources.quote: PostgreSQL with full-text search for document storage
does not slow down search response times noticeably.

constraints.text: Scope must fit the backend engineer's six-week contribution and the company's single-project capacity.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.
capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

constraints.text: Text access and evaluation arrangements must respect the company's private-cloud environment and internal security policy; permitted researcher access needs agreement.

sources.quote: Docker and Kubernetes on a private cloud hosted in Serbia

constraints.text: The collaboration must provide text for annotation and evaluation and assign production integration explicitly: the researcher's stated delivery model is research artifacts, not a production-ready application.

sources.quote: Rajić has a clear preference for collaborations where the company shares text data for annotation and evaluation rather than expecting a fully deployed software product
his group produces annotated corpora, trained models, and technical reports rather than production-ready applications.

risks: The evidence demonstrates normalization and morphological analysis mainly on informal Serbian, not bidirectional transliteration for contract retrieval or PostgreSQL integration. The first experiment must test this transfer on actual contract-query pairs before selecting an approach.
Normalization may conflate distinct terms, names, or ambiguous Latin sequences, increasing false matches even if zero-hit searches decline.
The reported one-in-five failure estimate comes from a January 2024 log sample; its current prevalence and attribution specifically to script mismatch remain unverified.
Researcher availability is unknown. Limited backend time and the researcher's non-production delivery model could leave integration, reindexing, or rollout unfinished.
Access to representative contracts and search logs, annotation permissions, and collaboration budget are unknown; any of these could block evaluation.
Latency and index-size overhead may make an otherwise linguistically effective approach unsuitable for the deployed search workload.
questions: Can Rajić commit time within the backend engineer's six-week window, and who will perform annotation and error adjudication?
What budget and deliverables are agreed, and who owns production implementation, reindexing, testing, and rollout?
Can representative contracts, queries, and known matching documents be made available for evaluation, under what access, pseudonymisation, retention, and publication conditions?
What are the current PostgreSQL configuration, tokenization rules, corpus size, query load, and search-latency baseline? What numerical latency and retrieval-quality thresholds define acceptance?
Which concrete Latin–Cyrillic ambiguities occur in the contracts, and how should names, foreign words, diacritics, and mixed-script tokens be treated?
Can the January 2024 finding be rechecked on recent logs, distinguishing script mismatch from parsing, tokenization, and other causes of zero hits?
Can the company support a controlled reindexing and rollback experiment within its private-cloud environment?
